sections.h2: Where deeds and mortgages are filed
sections.html:
Florida's 67 counties each keep separate Official Records under the county clerk. Whatever is filed there, whether a deed, a mortgage or a lien, can be searched by the public. The clerk also takes the deed stamp tax at the counter.

No statewide index exists. Search the Official Records of the county where the parcel sits, then turn to the property appraiser's website for the owner name, parcel number and assessed value.

sections.h2: Why filing a deed matters to a buyer
sections.html:
An unfiled deed leaves the buyer exposed. Under section 695.01, a conveyance, transfer or mortgage of real property, or a lease running a year or more, has no effect against creditors and later good-faith purchasers without notice unless it is filed as the law requires.

The same section treats a quitclaim grantee as a purchaser without notice under the recording acts. A lien from a government or quasi-government body for an improvement, service, fine or penalty binds later purchasers only when recorded. Tax, special assessment and utility liens are carved out.

Agents are covered too. A deed or mortgage signed under a power of attorney is not effective against creditors or later purchasers unless the power of attorney was recorded before their rights arose. If you are selling for an owner who cannot sign, record the power of attorney first.

Layout rules in section 695.26 are strict enough that a nonconforming deed may be refused at the recording desk. That can push back a closing by days.

  • Every signer's name typed or printed under the signature, with a mailing address.
  • Who prepared the paper, with a mailing address.
  • Printed names and addresses for each witness.
  • A printed name under any notary's signature.
  • Blank margin boxes at the top right: 3 by 3 inches on page one, 1 by 3 inches on later pages.
  • Each grantee's name and mailing address, except on a mortgage.

Exempt from these rules: wills, plats, court orders, papers signed by public officers, instruments dated before July 1, 1991 and instruments signed outside Florida. A page the clerk accepts despite a defect stays recorded.

Florida wants two people watching the signature. A written conveyance of a freehold, or of a term longer than one year, needs two subscribing witnesses (s. 689.01). Nobody needs a seal, and the witnessing can be done by audio-video link.

Quitclaim and lady bird deeds fall under the same rule. Leave a witness out and a title insurer may balk later.

A closing statement shows two kinds of charge: the clerk's page fees and stamp tax. The page fees come from s. 28.24.

Clerk charges in s. 28.24 for instruments up to 14 by 8.5 inches
ChargeAmount
Page one$5.00
Every added page$4.00
Each name past the fourth$1.00
Records modernization trust fund$1.00 page one, $0.50 per added page
Technology add-on$4 per page
Tax deed application handling$60.00

Page count and the number of names drive the total. Call the clerk's recording desk for a figure on your actual document.

Documentary stamp tax on a deed runs 70 cents per $100 of consideration (s. 201.02(1)(a)). Consideration is broad: cash, a released obligation, and any mortgage or encumbrance on the land, assumed or not.

Miami-Dade works differently, at 60 cents per $100 with a 45 cents per $100 surtax that falls away for paper moving only a single-family home. Everywhere else the 70 cents applies per $100 or portion thereof.

  • Each party to the paper is liable, even when the contract assigns payment to one side.
  • Taxable paper that never gets recorded is reported to the state revenue agency.
  • Taxable deed types: warranty, special warranty, quit claim, trustee's, life estate, contract for deed, deed in lieu, certificate of title.
  • A mortgage or note pays 35 cents per $100 secured, capped at $2,450 for the note tax.

Some paper escapes the tax. Under a probated will, the fiduciary's deed is not taxable. Section 201.02(7) exempts a spousal homestead deed whose only consideration is a mortgage, along with a divorce deed for the marital home.

Estate planning earns no exemption by that label alone. In advisement TAA 20B4-004 (October 2020), a lady bird deed on its particular facts moved no present beneficial interest and so owed nothing, but different facts could produce a different answer.

Separately, nearly any title transfer is a change of ownership for Save Our Homes, and the next January 1 assessment goes back to just value. Before deeding a long-held homestead, talk to the property appraiser.

A parcel's paper trail is split among three elected offices. The clerk holds recorded instruments and takes deed stamp tax, the property appraiser sets just value each January 1 and rules on exemptions, and the tax collector bills and collects.

  • Clerk: deeds, mortgages, liens, tax deed and foreclosure sale paperwork.
  • Property appraiser: ownership on the roll, TRIM notice and exemption decisions.
  • Tax collector: November bills, delinquency, tax certificates.

Plat filings carry their own clerk charge in s. 28.24: $30.00 for the first page and $15.00 for each additional page. A surveyor or developer subdividing land should budget for that separately from deed recording.

sections.h2: Preparing a deed so it records the first time
sections.html:
Most rejections are about small things. Print each signer's name beneath the signature, add the preparer's name and mailing address, and give every witness a printed name and address. Leave the top right margin blank. Name each grantee with a mailing address, unless the paper is a mortgage.

Check the number of pages and names before you go to the recording desk, since both change the fee. If the sale is by an agent for an owner, make sure the recorded power of attorney is already in the file. A deed that records cleanly the first time saves a trip and keeps the closing date where it is.

sections.h2: Foreclosure and tax deed sales on the record
sections.html:
Mortgages and liens appear in a title search and need a payoff or release before a clean deed can pass. A foreclosure sale ends in a certificate of title, on which tax is figured from the highest and best bid under s. 201.02(9).

A tax deed buyer owes stamp tax and recording fees within 24 hours of the auction, excluding weekends and holidays. A recorded contract-for-deed vendee is among the parties the tax collector notifies before that sale, which shows how recording protects an installment buyer.

sections.h2: Reviewing the records before you list
sections.html:
Order copies of the vesting deed, every recorded mortgage and any lien. They show what has to be paid at closing and whether the name on title is the name of the person who will sign.

When you got the house through an estate, a gift or an unusual deed, check with the recording desk about what it will take before picking a closing date.

Watch for government liens imposed for a fine or penalty. Section 695.01(3) makes them valid against later buyers only when a notice of lien was recorded naming the owner of record, a description or address, and the parcel number. If one sits on your parcel, study it carefully before signing a listing agreement.

Even with cash buyers there is no lender timeline to wait on, yet the title search still runs the same way. The records you pull now are what set the closing date.

faqs.q: Which office takes deeds for recording in Florida?
faqs.a: Go to the clerk serving the land's county. Stamp tax is paid at that same counter, which is why the deed has to meet the form rules first.

Page count and the number of names. The first page costs more than later ones, names beyond the fourth add a charge, and trust fund and technology fees ride on top (s. 28.24(13)). The clerk will quote a total.

faqs.q: Is the stamp rate identical in all 67 counties?
faqs.a: Almost. Miami-Dade works from a separate formula, 60 cents per $100 plus a surtax of 45 cents that single-family transfers escape. Elsewhere it is 70 cents per $100.
Not between the signers. Section 695.01, though, strips its effect against creditors and later buyers for value who lack notice. Stamp tax applies to a deed whether or not it gets recorded.

faqs.q: Do the layout rules reach every instrument?
faqs.a: No. Wills, plats, court orders, papers signed by public officers and instruments signed outside Florida are exempt. A clerk may also take a page with odd name placement when it is clear who signed.
